In the present second edition the book has been thoroughly revised and brought in conformity with the new curriculum. Select poems are included in the book along with the new ones. New prose additions are those adopted from standard literatures. The language used in the book is considered to be standard from the view-point of style and expression. Modern thoughts and ideas are expressed in easy, lucid and appropriate

language. The book has been all along prepared with an eye to meeting the needs of a moral class-book be- sides the supply of standard Khasi literature which is the urgent need of the day. A glance at the table of contentsjwill convince any keen observer of the fact that the subject-matters have been well selected to supply the present demand- the demand to build up, through reading lessons* the moral character of the young generation of the present age. Every lover of our country’s welfare is to read this book for himself. This book has been prescribed by the Department for class VII and VIII from the year 1050 to 1954 and for class VII for 1955 and 1956 ; and its selections were prescribed for class IV in 1964. Second and Enlarged Edition. Published by the Author, AU rights reserved. Printed at the K. J. Presbyterian Press, Shillong. ^ PREFACE TO THE REVISED EDITION. In the present second edition the book has been thoroughly revised and brought in conformity with the new curriculum. Select poems are included in the book along with the new ones. New prose additions are those adopted from standard literatures. The language used in the book is considered to be standard from the view-point of style and expression. Modern thoughts and ideas are expressed in easy, lucid and appropriate

language. The book has been all along prepared with an eye to meeting the needs of a moral class-book be- sides the supply of standard Khasi literature which is the urgent need of the day. A glance at the table of contentsjwill convince any keen observer of the fact that the subject-matters have been well selected to supply the present demand- the demand to build up, through reading lessons* the moral character of the young generation of the present age. Every lover of our country’s welfare is to read this book for himself. This book has been prescribed by the Department for class VII and VIII from the year 1050 to 1954 and for class VII for 1955 and 1956 ; and its selections were prescribed for class IV in 1964. Badhakrishna says that teachers who are setters of learning and propagators of truths form the intellec- tual conscience of our community.” Shillong : July 1056.
